deals.evidence: Manchester City will be the majority owner, according to the league's announcement
deals.headline: MLS awards 20th expansion club to Manchester City and the New York Yankees
deals.investor: Manchester City (City Football Group) and New York Yankees
deals.summary: MLS announced Manchester City (majority owner) and the New York Yankees would acquire its 20th expansion club, New York City FC. Pre-2015; listed for context.

deals.evidence: values the team’s holding company at about US$1.5 billion
deals.headline: Marcelo Claure buys about 10% of NYCFC's parent at a reported ~$1.5bn valuation
deals.summary: Claure took approximately 10% of City Football Group US Holdco LLC (club plus future stadium) and became Co-Vice Chairman; CFG 80%, Yankee Global Enterprises ~10%, Claure ~10% afterwards. SportsPro, citing Sportico, reports the holding company valued at about $1.5bn.

deals.evidence: J.P. Morgan arranged private financing for the stadium.
deals.headline: NYCFC breaks ground on privately financed $780m Etihad Park
deals.summary: Groundbreaking of the 25,000-seat Etihad Park at Willets Point, Queens, privately financed (J.P. Morgan arranged the financing), projected to open for the 2027 MLS season. $780m is the stadium cost as stated by a speaker, not the financing amount.

honours.evidence: the Club went on to be crowned 2021 MLS Cup Champions for the first time in Club history.

legal_entity.evidence: City Football Group US Holdco LLC, which has combined ownership over New York City FC and the Club’s future stadium in Willets Point, Queens.
legal_entity.name: City Football Group US Holdco LLC (parent of the club and its stadium)

operating_result.source_name: Forbes (estimate), The Most Valuable MLS Teams 2026

stadium_owner.detail: Plays most home games at Yankee Stadium, home of minority owner the New York Yankees. Its own 25,000-seat Etihad Park is privately financed (J.P. Morgan arranged the financing) and owned through City Football Group US Holdco LLC with the club.
stadium_owner.evidence: NYCFC plays the majority of home games at the iconic Yankee Stadium, which is also home to minority owner, the New York Yankees.

founded_evidence: New York City Football Club came into existence as Major League Soccer’s 20th franchise on May 21, 2013
name: New York City Football Club
notes: The earlier record's valuation ($875m via si.com) is replaced by Forbes 2026 ($1.02bn, +17%); Forbes is cited via its Internet Archive snapshot (original 403s). Revenue and operating income are Forbes estimates for 2025 (EBITDA basis). Stakes are 'approximately' per the club's release. The $780m Etihad Park figure is the stadium's cost as quoted in the club's release, the financing size is not stated. No Yankee Stadium soccer capacity, attendance, socials, sponsor or chair found on a citable page. Silver Lake and Newton are indirect holders via CFG (stakes in CFG, not in NYCFC).

owners.name: Silver Lake (indirect, through City Football Group)

owners.evidence: CFG is majority owned by Newton Investment and Development LLC, fully owned by His Highness Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan
owners.name: Newton Investment and Development LLC (Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan; indirect, through City Football Group)

ownership_summary: The parent, City Football Group US Holdco LLC (which owns the club and its future Willets Point stadium), is 80% owned by City Football Group, with Yankee Global Enterprises and Marcelo Claure each holding about 10% since Claure's investment in September 2024. City Football Group itself is majority owned by Sheikh Mansour's Newton Investment and Development LLC, with Silver Lake holding nearly 17%.
